title: Auth middleware
idea: `verifyJWT` is middleware that proves who is calling. It reads the access token, verifies it, loads the user and sets `req.user` before the controller runs.
points: The token comes from the `accessToken` cookie, or a `Bearer` header for API clients.
`jwt.verify` checks signature and expiry with `ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET`, and throws on failure.
It then loads the user by the token's `_id`, leaving out hashes and tokens.
Every failure becomes `ApiError(401)`; `next()` runs only on success.

steps.caption: A request reaches a secured route. `verifyJWT` runs before the controller.
It looks for a token: the `accessToken` cookie first, then an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
No token at all ends the request with `401`.
A token is found. `jwt.verify` checks its signature and expiry.
A forged or expired token makes `jwt.verify` throw. The middleware answers `401`.
A valid token names a user id. The middleware loads that user, without secret fields.
The account was deleted: no document, so `401` even though the token verified.
User found: it becomes `req.user` and `next()` runs.

code.caption: Trimmed to this lesson's file, with stand-ins above it. Press Run: six requests, one of them for a deleted user.

walk.text: Demo values and condensed earlier files, so the program runs alone.
The fields to leave out: the password hash and every stored token.
Cookie first, else a `Bearer` header. No token means `401`.
`jwt.verify` throws on a bad signature or an expired token. Turn that into `401`.
Load the user without secrets. No user means `401`; otherwise set `req.user`.
Try each case. The last request uses a valid token for a deleted user.

pitfalls: Register `cookieParser()` before your routers, or `req.cookies` is `undefined`.
Look the user up on every request: a valid token can outlive its account.
Exclude `password` and token fields with `select`, or `req.user` leaks them.

quiz.why: The token still verifies, but `findById` returns `null`, so the middleware throws `ApiError(401)`.

takeaway: A signed token proves identity; the database proves the account still exists.

starters: Why accept both a cookie and a Bearer header?
Should the middleware tell an expired token from a forged one?
Where does `verifyJWT` go in a route's chain?
